name: Bound keys only: the setting, its audited switch, and a preview that says what it did not decide
summary: The setting bound_keys_only (deployment.private.json; absent or false is off) makes the forced command of an authorized_keys line refuse a line that lacks a project or a principal; the switch (status/on/off, operator-gated, audited, off) previews what on would cut off, by ONE rule in three groups. REFUSED: a command needing no shell (a plain-character whitelist), this kit's own wrapper by absolute path, this root, parsed unbound - would_be_refused (twenty numbers, _more, truncated) in status, on, the listing. MAY BE REFUSED: every OTHER line with a command= - another wrapper or root, shell syntax, a relative or ~ path, another program - printed by status and on as may_be_refused with _more, printing both groups BEFORE it writes, wrapper_names_setting saying as a HINT whether the wrapper names the setting in its first 64 KiB of the OPEN descriptor (once per file; a fifo never opened); a word in a file is a hint, not a decision. Another-reason lines are refused either way; only a no-command line is outside. on REFUSES to flip when the keys file cannot be read or was only partly inspected unless --without-preview is said; a NUL or over-long wrapper path costs one line.
